newsitem.title: UK: Indonesian 1997 sugar output seen at 2.55 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian 1997 sugar output seen at 2.55 mln T.

text.p: Indonesia's sugar output could reach 2.55 million tonnes in 1997 and rise to over 3.0 million by the year 2000 if a production development plan is met, the Indonesian Sugar Association chairman said on Wednesday.

In a speech prepared for a seminar hosted by the International Sugar Organization (ISO), Faruk Bakrie said a projected expansion of sugar mills outside Java would expand the region's contribution to total national output.
He cited five mills in Sumatera, two in Sulawesi and three respectively in Nusa Tenggara, Irian and East Timor.
Indonesia produced 2.10 million tonnes of sugar in 1995, Bakrie said, with Java accounting for 74 percent of the total.
Java's dominant share of the national sugar output was expected to dwindle to around 40 percent by the year 2003, Bakrie said.
"The distribution of geographical structure may contribute a positive impact to the efficient distribution and marketing of the sugar," he said.
